These can be Claim Data or Echart or\npat Notes.\n• EXT refers to the file extension of the resulting exported data. Extensions are XML\n(accompanied by a HTML file) and CSV (comma separated values data).\nThe files are further categorized as follows:\n1. Patient Demographics and Clinical Data – HL7 C-CDA formatted\n2. Adhoc Patient Notes such as documented telephone calls – CSV formatted\n3. Scanned Records – HL7 CDA formatted.\nFormat of the resulting EHI Export Files\nIn order to successfully use or import the exported EHI files, the user must understand the formatting of\nthe resulting files.\n\nPatient Demographics and Clinical Data\nThe resulting files follows the specification as set for HL7 C-CDA R2.1 specifications. These files\nwill always result in a pair following an XML and HTML file extension. It must be noted there will NOT be\na TYPE value in the filename. This data is categorized as PHI and is included within\nEHI. The resulting files are formatted using comma-separated values also known as CSV. This file will\nfollow an CSV file extension. It must be noted there will be a TYPE value called patNotes within the\nfilename. The format and descriptors are described in the following table:\n\nColumn Number\n\nColumn Name\n\nDescription\n\n1\n\nPID\n\n2\n\nPatient Notes ID\n\n3\n\nUsername\n\n3\n\nSubject\n\n4\n\nPatient Notes Category\n\n5\n\nPatient Notes Date\n\n6\n\nPatient Notes\n\nData reflected under this column are patient IDs.\nThese are unique.\nData reflected under this column are patient note\nIDs. These are unique.\nData reflected under this column refer to the user\nwho documented the note\nData reflected under this column refer to the\nsubject of the note. This field maybe blank\nData reflected under this column refers to the\ncategory associated with the note. These\ncategories are user defined but available from a\npick list for the user.\nData reflected under this column refer to the date\nthe note was created.\nData reflected under this column refers to\ndocumented details of the patient note.\n\nScanned Records\nThe resulting files follow the specification as set for HL7 C-CDA R2.1 specifications. This file will\nfollow an XML file extension. It must be noted there will be a TYPE value called Echart within the\nfilename. This file contains all patient scanned and uploaded documents and is coded using Base64\nencoding. It must be noted, this file could be large in size depending on the amount of scanned data. The CSV has 6 columns:\n   - PID (Patient ID)\n   - Patient Notes ID\n   - Username (who documented the note)\n   - Subject (may be blank)\n   - Patient Notes Category (user-defined, from a pick list)\n   - Patient Notes Date\n   - Patient Notes (the actual note content)\n\n3. **Scanned Records** — HL7 CDA formatted XML files containing Base64-encoded scanned/uploaded documents. Filename includes an \"Echart\" TYPE indicator. If ezPractice performs the export on the user's behalf, fees may apply based on time and effort.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe export documentation describes three categories of exported data: C-CDA clinical data, adhoc patient notes (CSV), and scanned records (CDA). Notably, the file naming convention mentions \"Claim Data\" as one of the TYPE values, suggesting billing/claims data is part of the export even though it is not described in detail in the documentation.\n\n**Likely covered (via C-CDA R2.1):**\n- Patient demographics\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Problems/diagnoses\n- Lab results\n- Vital signs\n- Immunizations\n- Procedures\n- Clinical notes (to the extent included in C-CDA sections)\n\n**Covered via separate files:**\n- Adhoc patient notes (CSV) — telephone calls, miscellaneous notes\n- Scanned/uploaded documents (CDA with Base64 encoding)\n- Claim data (mentioned in filename convention as a TYPE, but not described further)\n\n**Unclear or potentially missing:**\n- **Billing records** — \"Claim Data\" is mentioned as a TYPE value in the filename convention, suggesting it's exported, but the documentation provides no detail on its format, fields, or structure. This is a significant gap in the documentation, not necessarily in the export itself.\n- **CPOE orders** — Medication orders, lab orders, and imaging orders are key certified features. Someone receiving claim data files would have no documentation to interpret them.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a mixed format approach:\n- **C-CDA R2.1** for clinical data — a well-established healthcare standard. This is appropriate for demographics and clinical summaries but inherently limited to what C-CDA sections cover. C-CDA is a clinical document standard, not a complete database export format.\n- **CSV** for adhoc patient notes — simple and interpretable, with column descriptions provided.\n- **CDA with Base64** for scanned records — standard approach for encoded document attachments.\n\nThe C-CDA format means clinical data export is constrained to what C-CDA sections support. The documentation simply points to the C-CDA R2.1 specification rather than documenting which C-CDA sections are populated or how ezPractice-specific data maps to C-CDA elements.\n\nA third party could reasonably process the C-CDA files (since C-CDA is a well-known standard) and the patient notes CSV (since column descriptions are provided).
